in_english.name: Dhahi
in_english.meaning: one who travels, migrates, or carries something, future, caller, bearer
in_english.long_meaning: The name Dhahi is derived from the Arabic root د-ح-ي (d-h-y), which means to travel, migrate, or carry something. In Islamic tradition, Dhahi refers to the Prophet Muhammad and his companions who migrated from Mecca to Medina. The name also symbolizes the concept of future and the idea of carrying or conveying something. In Arabic, the word ذاهب (dhaahib) means one who travels or migrates, while ذاهٍ (dhaahin) means one who carries or conveys something. The name Dhahi is also associated with the idea of calling or summoning, as in the phrase 'dhaahin al-mu'jib' (one who answers the call). In Islamic culture, the name Dhahi is considered a symbol of spiritual journey and the quest for knowledge.

The name encourages us to be like the flowing water, always giving and never resisting in the flow of life, and to remain steadfast in our faith and devotion to Allah.
